the model is able to predict the pressure drop and LMTD of fluted tube condensers using R-407C with a good level of accuracy.
the fluted tube condensing model of Rousseau et  al. (2003), which was developed for single component refrigerants, can be extended to R-407C with reasonable accuracy.
the model can be used to accurately predict the performance of R-407C in fluted tube condensers.

the development of an improved fluted tube condensers model that can be used with refrigerant mixtures.
improving the accuracy of the model for the condensation of refrigerant R- 407C in fluted tube annular heat exchangers.
the applicability of a fluted tube condensation model when applied to refrigerant R- 407C.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the fluted tube-in-tubes condenser model developed by Rousseau et  al. (2013) is applicable for the condensation of R-407C in the fluted tube annulus.
the model is applicable when used with the new enhancement factors for condensing R-407C inside fluted tube-in-tubes.
the model is applicable to condensation inside flutes for R-407A, R-407C, R-134a, R-22, R-717, R-1234yf and R-1234ze(E) and that the new enhancement factors are applicable to R-407A and R-407C.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the model is capable of accurately predicting the performance of fluted tubes for condensing R-407C.
the model is applicable for R-407 condensation in fluted tube heat exchangers, provided that the new enhancement factors are implemented.
the model is applicable for the prediction of the performance of fluted tube condensers using R-407C as the working fluid.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the model developed by Rousseau et  al. (2003), which was originally developed for pure refrigerants, can be extended to simulate zeotropic refrigerants with reasonable accuracy.
the model developed by Rousseau et al. (2003), can be used to simulate condensation inside flutes for R-407 C with an accuracy that is acceptable for most engineering applications.
the model developed by Rousseau et  al. (2003) is suitable for simulating condensation of zeotropic mixtures in fluted tube condensers.
